missionPremise: cortex-api does not boot. A canary deploy of 5688aa31 failed with Cloud Run 'container failed to start and listen on PORT=8080'. Dispatched by the doc_repo planner under OPS-16 amendment A-020 (2026-08-19). Operating law for the lane is 61_enforcement_doctrine revision 7 and enforcement.mdc, both read at 'P:/tmp/data fix/' under their real names '61_enforcement_doctrine (7).md' and 'enforcement (3).mdc'; the unsuffixed paths named in the dispatch do not exist.

defectReproduced.how: pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server run build at 5688aa31, then node --enable-source-maps ./dist/index.mjs with a complete boot env

dispatchCorrection.claim: The dispatch states the chain as countyCoverageScoreCli.ts:115 'import { argv } from node:process' plus countyCoverageScoreCli.ts:183 'process.exit(1)', i.e. the module evaluates at import and exits.
dispatchCorrection.verifiedAtSource: Line 183 sits inside function fail(), not at top level. The CLI DOES carry an entrypoint guard at line 1156, 'if (isDirectRun())'. isDirectRun() compares realpathSync(argv[1]) against realpathSync(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)).
dispatchCorrection.actualMechanism: esbuild bundles every module into dist/index.mjs, so inside the bundle import.meta.url IS the bundle's own URL. The container runs 'node artifacts/api-server/dist/index.mjs', so argv[1] is that same path. isDirectRun() therefore returns TRUE at server boot, main() runs, process.argv.slice(2) is empty, and main() reaches fail('pass --county=<fips> or --all') which calls process.exit(1) before Express listens.
dispatchCorrection.whyThisMatters: A fix aimed only at the argv import or at the process.exit line would change nothing. The guard is not missing; it is defeated by bundling. artifacts/api-server/src/lib/nodeFacetTier2Constants.ts already records this in its header: the entrypoint guard 'is unreliable in the production bundle'. The only fix that holds is removing the CLI from the boot graph.

competingMechanismsForTheSameObservation.mechanism: A missing or invalid boot env var. The server's own fail-fast validators call process.exit(1) on unset secrets.
competingMechanismsForTheSameObservation.rejectedBecause: It was hit twice on the way here and each time produced a different, differently worded exit (SNAPSHOT_SECRET refusal, then an AI_INTEGRATIONS_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL throw). Supplying those advanced the failure rather than removing it. The final observed failure carries the coverage-score message with a full env supplied.

competingMechanismsForTheSameObservation.mechanism: Some other module's top-level side effect exiting the process.
competingMechanismsForTheSameObservation.rejectedBecause: The literal string '[coverage-score]' is emitted only by countyCoverageScoreCli.ts across the whole tree, and on the empty-argv path that string is reachable only through fail() from main(), which is called only from the isDirectRun() block.

competingMechanismsForTheSameObservation.mechanism: Cloud Run cold-start timeout or memory pressure, i.e. a slow boot rather than an exited one.
competingMechanismsForTheSameObservation.rejectedBecause: Reproduced locally with no Cloud Run involved. The process exits 1 within seconds. A timeout would leave the process alive.

fix.shape: Extract the pure classification surface into a side-effect-free leaf module, mirroring the precedent at src/lib/nodeFacetTier2Constants.ts, and repoint every consumer at it. No re-export is left behind on the CLI, so the hazardous import path cannot be reintroduced by habit.
fix.whyNotMoved: They read COUNTY_RAIL_DECLARATION from @workspace/db/schema. Nothing in the boot graph imports them; only countyCoverageRailState.test.ts does. Moving them would widen the change without removing any hazard.
fix.typeOnlyDependency: The moved types reference JoinIntegrityReport['verdict'] from ./joinIntegrityGate, which imports @workspace/cad-ingest. It is taken as a statement-level 'import type', which esbuild erases, so no runtime edge is created. Duplicating the verdict union locally was rejected: that is the two-definitions-disagreeing shape the railScoring engine header exists to prevent.

controls.shape: A Node harness that spawns the already-built bundle, polls the port, and kills the child under a hard deadline in a finally block.
controls.threeOutcomes: pass exit 0 / violation exit 1 / GATE-DID-NOT-RUN exit 2 with a loud marker. Tooling fails LOUD, not closed.
controls.selfTest: Runs its own predicate against a fixture entry that exits without listening (must be flagged) and a fixture entry that listens (must pass) before any verdict on the real bundle is trusted. Mirrors the ci-tier2-flood-not-served idiom already in pr-checks.yml.
controls.violationProof: Run against unfixed 5688aa31 and shown FAILING before the fix. A real production-main violation, not a simulated one.

controls.shape: An import-graph walker rooted at src/index.ts that follows static relative imports and flags any reached module matching *Cli.ts, printing the full path from the root.
controls.whyAGraphWalkAndNotAGrep: The live defect reaches the CLI through the lib/railScoring/index.ts BARREL: routes/countyRailScore.ts imports ../lib/railScoring, which re-exports ./engine, which imports ../../countyCoverageScoreCli. A per-file grep over routes/ finds nothing. Re-export through an intermediate module is named in the dispatch as the obvious bypass of a grep, so the control is built not to have it.
controls.selfTest: Two fixture trees, one violating and one clean, both walked on every run.

adversarialReviewOfThisDesign.risk: The boot smoke test could pass for the wrong reason, e.g. an entry that listens but is not the real server.
adversarialReviewOfThisDesign.mitigation: The real run targets dist/index.mjs by path and the harness prints the entry it ran and the commit. Fixtures are used only in the self-test phase and are reported separately.

adversarialReviewOfThisDesign.risk: The boot smoke test needs a reachable database and would then be testing the database rather than boot.
adversarialReviewOfThisDesign.mitigation: DATABASE_URL is pointed at an unreachable local port on purpose. If boot cannot complete without a live DB, that is itself a finding and will be reported rather than papered over by adding a postgres service.

adversarialReviewOfThisDesign.risk: The smoke env uses dummy secrets, so it can diverge from the real deploy env and miss a boot failure only production sees.
adversarialReviewOfThisDesign.mitigation: Stated as a scope limit rather than claimed away. The harness proves the process reaches listen with a well-formed env. It does not prove the production secret set is correct.

adversarialReviewOfThisDesign.risk: The graph walker over-approximates. An inline 'import { type X } from ./fooCli' is erased by esbuild but would still be flagged.
adversarialReviewOfThisDesign.mitigation: Accepted and documented. It errs toward flagging, and the remedy (write 'import type') is the correct form anyway. A control that under-flags is the failure mode this lane exists for.

adversarialReviewOfThisDesign.risk: Both controls are CI checks in a repo whose main is not branch-protected, so neither blocks anything.
adversarialReviewOfThisDesign.mitigation: Not mitigated. Reported as the sixth state, advisory, in the close, per doctrine revision 7.

constraintsHonored: Isolated worktree P:/tmp/ss-w18-boot-fix. No other lane's tree touched.
Every verification step exit-bounded. No watch, no tail -f, no non-exiting server.
No merge and no deploy. Both are planner-owned.
Commit under test declared in every output.
openAtCP1: Whether the server can reach app.listen with an unreachable DATABASE_URL. Unknown at CP1 because the CLI exit happens during module evaluation, before bootAndListen() is ever reached.
Whether the graph walk flags anything besides the known defect.
